relations.myth: Yahweh condemns Solomon’s worship of Milcom
relations.note: Yahweh condemns Milcom’s worship and announces the division of Solomon’s kingdom.
Both deities are objects of Solomon’s apostasy but never interact directly.

relations.myth: Foreign gods condemned during Solomon’s apostasy
relations.note: Milcom and Chemosh appear as neighboring national gods condemned alongside Astarte.
Their Jerusalem high places are jointly listed among those desecrated by Josiah.
Their neighboring Jerusalem high places are desecrated together during Josiah’s reform.

relations.myth: Molech substitutes for Milcom in Solomon’s apostasy
relations.note: The Masoretic reading may substitute Molech for Milcom; other witnesses and passages distinguish them.
Modern scholars propose Milcom as El’s Ammonite royal title or an assimilated deity.
MLKM and QWS occur together in a bilingual inscription, if MLKM denotes Milcom.
MLKM and KMS occur together in a bilingual inscription, if both identifications are correct.
